items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I said to Charlie Rause, I says, 'I don't know what the hell I'm gonna do.' ... Charlie said to me, 'I'm not worried about you, you're a good hustler.'

ctx.x: We started talking about what are you ever gonna do.

Oh yeah, that was it. I said to Charlie Rause, I says, "I don't know what the hell I'm gonna do." I lost my club in Boston and I don't have the festival – there had been a riot. And I says, I'm doing these things…. Charlie said to me, "I'm not worried about you, you're a good hustler." And he meant that in a, you know, like a good hustler, like a baseball player that runs out everything. And that was … he understood that. So I guess I'm a good hustler. I don't know.

Well, you've certainly not only fashioned an amazing career for yourself, but you've catapulted many people into their own lime lights, both artistry and otherwise. I'm wondering who are some of the standouts for you are.
